_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with acromegaly who had an inadequate response to surgery and/or for whom surgery is not an option

pivotal_trials.population: Adults with biochemically uncontrolled acromegaly, treatment naïve or previously treated on a somatostatin analog and washed out
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of participants achieving biochemical control (IGF-1 level ≤ 1.0 × ULN) at Week 24 versus placebo
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 24, 56% of PALSONIFY participants achieved biochemical control vs 5% of placebo (p < 0.0001)

pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acromegaly previously biochemically controlled on injectable depot octreotide or lanreotide
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of participants with biochemical response (IGF-1 ≤ 1.0 × ULN) at Week 36 versus placebo
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 36, 83% of PALSONIFY participants maintained biochemical control vs 4% of placebo (p < 0.0001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, decreased appetite, sinus bradycardia, hyperglycemia, palpitations, and gastroenteritis; cholelithiasis and complications reported in 6% of participants
target_moa: Selective somatostatin receptor 2 (SSTR2) agonist that suppresses GH and IGF-1 secretion

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug designation for the treatment of acromegaly, granted July 7, 2020

citations.quote: Paltusotine was granted *Orphan Drug* designation for the treatment of acromegaly by the Office of Orphan Products Development on July 7, 2020 (#DRU-2017-5766).

summary.text: Standard review NDA supported by two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials; paltusotine held Orphan Drug designation for acromegaly.

citations.quote: This NDA includes data from two randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trials to provide substantial evidence of the safety and efficacy of paltusotine in patients with acromegaly.
Paltusotine was granted *Orphan Drug* designation for the treatment of acromegaly by the Office of Orphan Products Development on July 7, 2020 (#DRU-2017-5766).
